project.name: profiles
project.title: profiles
project.summary: A thread-safe cache of configuration profiles loaded on first use from a pluggable backing store.

contract: Registry is shared between threads. get(name) returns the cached profile when there is one. Otherwise it loads the settings from the source, caches the new profile and returns it; a name the source does not know returns None and caches nothing. Two threads that miss at the same time may both call load, but the first insert wins and both receive the same Arc. Any name is accepted, including the empty string.

/// A named list of settings, shared between threads through `Arc`.
/// Backing store for profiles, for example a directory of files.

check.summary: A worker thread calls get on an empty registry for a known name, again for the same name, and for an unknown name; the main thread waits three seconds for the results, then four threads request one more name concurrently.
check.failure_signature: CHECK-FAIL: get did not return within 3 s on a cache miss

label.trigger: Any call for a name that is not cached yet. The MutexGuard created in the match scrutinee lives until the end of the whole match, so the None arm calls lock() on a mutex its own thread still holds.
label.expected_impact: The first lookup of every profile blocks its thread for good (std's Mutex is not reentrant). Every other thread that touches the registry then waits on the same lock, so the worker pool stalls on startup.

known_counterevidence.note: Binding the cloned Arc in its own statement ends the temporary guard at the semicolon, so the second lock() in the miss path is uncontended and load runs without the lock.
The entry().or_insert() insert is the correct way to honour the first-insert-wins rule; it is not the problem.

label.reviewer_notes: Cached hits work, so only the miss path shows it. The borrow checker accepts the code. A report that only says the lock is held while load runs is the same root cause and should count, provided it reaches the re-lock in the None arm.
